title: Quran Study 1
content:
Quick Notes for Quran Study 1 - Study Information 

● Study Leaders: Catherine (lead teacher for the session) and Dr. Rashad 
Khalifa (provides extensive commentary, answers questions, and leads the 
second half). 
● Date of Recording: 05/26/1989 

Quran Verses Discussed 
● Sura 72 (The Jinn): Verses 19–28 
● Sura 73 (The Cloaked): Verses 1–20 
● Reference Verses: 
○ Sura 74:30-31 (Regarding the number 19 and angels) 
○ Sura 67:8 (Guards of Hell) 
○ Sura 43:77 (Maalik, the angel of Hell) 
○ Sura 53:43-48 (God controls happiness and wealth) 
○ Sura 1 (Al-Fatihah - recited at the end) 

Detailed Summary of Discussion 
1. Sura 72:19–28 (The Jinn) 
● The Message of "God Alone": 
○ Theme: The core message of all messengers is "Worship God Alone." 
○ Reaction to the Message: When God alone is advocated, the hearts of 
disbelievers "shrink in aversion." This is described as a literal 
shrinking of the soul (ego gets in the way). 
○ Messengers are Human: Messengers (Noah, Moses, Jesus, Rashad) are 
human beings with no power to harm or guide. They possess no 
"superhuman" claims or magic. Their humanity is a test for the people, 
who often reject them asking, "Who are you? You are just a man." 
● Protection of Messengers: While messengers are vulnerable due to their high 
visibility and the specific proofs they carry, they are protected by God as long 
as they deliver the message. 
● The Unforgivable Sin: Idol worship is the only unforgivable sin (if maintained 
until death). 
● Majority vs. Minority (Spiritual Physics): 
○ The "Shrinking" Concept: Dr. Khalifa explains that while a human 
body looks the same, the soul varies wildly in size based on belief. 
○ Statistics: In a city like Tucson (approx. 500,000 people), there might 
be only 50-100 true believers. 

○ Size comparison: A believer's soul is described as being as large as a 
city (e.g., Phoenix), while a disbeliever's soul shrinks to the size of an 
ant or cat. 
○ Conclusion: Therefore, 100 believers are physically/spiritually the 
"majority" in power compared to 500,000 "ants." 
● Knowledge of the Future: 
○ Only God knows the future. He reveals specific news to chosen 
messengers to authenticate them. 
○ Examples given: Joseph knowing his family would bow to him; Moses’ 
mother being told he would be saved. 
● The Number 19 & Hell: 
○ A debate arises regarding the number of angels guarding Hell. 
○ Dr. Khalifa’s Clarification: The Quran says "Over it is nineteen." It 
does not explicitly say "19 angels." It is a mathematical code/structure. 
The function of the number is a test for the disbelievers and certainty 
for believers. 

2. Sura 73:1–20 (The Cloaked) 
● Night Meditation: 
○ The night is designed for rest and lack of distraction, making it the 
ideal time for meditation and reading the Quran. 
○ Definition of Night: Quranic night begins at sunset and ends at dawn. 
○ Routine: Reading Quran and meditating is for the human's benefit, not 
God's need. 
● 24-Hour God Consciousness: 
○ The goal of the believer is to mention and remember God constantly 
(writing Bismillah on checks, saying it before tasks). 
○ God is the only Doer: Belief that God hires, fires, and provides. If one 
believes their boss provides for them, it is a form of idol worship. 
● Anger and Aggression: 
○ Core Teaching: Do not get angry. If someone upsets you or cuts you off 
in traffic, it is God testing you or you are paying for a past sin. 
○ Self-Defense: Discussion on whether to fight back. The consensus is 
that self-defense is a right (Sura 42), but patience and restraint are 
superior qualities. Dr. Khalifa notes, "It takes more strength to 
restrain yourself." 
○ Sadness vs. Anger: Being sad/depressed is viewed as "objecting" to 
God's will. 
● The End of the World: 

○ Date: Dr. Khalifa states the world will end in 2280 AD. 
○ Human History: Humanity is currently in its "infancy." Less than 7% 
of all humans destined to exist have come so far; 93% are yet to come. 
The message of the Quran and the mathematical code are being 
consolidated now for the vast majority of future humanity. 
● Geology and The Day of Judgment: 
○ Verse 14 mentions mountains turning to a "weightless pile." 
○ Dr. Khalifa references the molten core of the Earth, suggesting the 
solid ground is an illusion that will be shattered. 
○ Progeria Reference: Verse 17 mentions a day that makes "infants 
gray-haired." This is linked to the disease Progeria (rapid aging) as a 
metaphor for the brevity of life on Judgment Day. 

3. Administrative & Closing Notes 
● Missing Prayers: God is merciful regarding missed night prayers due to 
illness, travel, or business (seeking provisions). However, Dr. Khalifa 
emphasizes never missing the Dawn (Fajr) prayer. 
● Virginity Appendix: Dr. Khalifa announces a new appendix for the 
translation titled "Virginity," urging parents to teach children to save 
themselves for their spouses. 
● Next Session: Dr. Sabahi will take over the next week to discuss the Farsi 
translation (Suras 74, 75, 76). 
● Al-Fatihah: The group recites Al-Fatihah for the birthdays of Lydia, Hany, 
Douglas, and Amir, and for Mahvash's upcoming trip to Iran. 
● Final Reminder: God controls happiness and wealth (referencing Sura 53). 
Following God's law guarantees a happy life.

title: Quran Study 2
content:
Quick Notes for Quran Study 2 - Study Information 

● Study Leader: Dr. Mahmoud Sabahi (Chemistry background, led the 
teaching). 
● Date of Recording: 08/04/1989 

Quran Verses Discussed 
● Sura 95 (The Fig): Verses 1–8 
● Sura 96 (The Embryo): Verses 1–19 
● Reference Verses: 
○ Sura 87 (Creation and shaping) 
○ Sura 93, 92, 100, 91, 81 (Referenced regarding God "swearing" by 
created things) 
○ Sura 1 (Al-Fatihah - recited at the end) 

Detailed Summary of Discussion 
1. Sura 95:1–8 (The Fig) 
● Swearing by Objects: 
○ Dr. Sabahi notes that there are approximately 12 Suras where God 
begins by swearing by created things (e.g., the Sun, Moon, Night, Day). 
○ Sura 95 is unique as it is the only one where God swears by plants (Fig 
and Olive). 
● Symbolism of the Plants and Locations: 
○ Dr. Khalifa explains the specific symbolism linking the verses to God's 
messengers: 
■ The Fig: Represents Adam (universal association with fig 
leaves/Paradise). 
■ The Olive: Represents Jesus (Mount of Olives). 
■ Mount Sinai: Represents Moses. 
■ The Honored Town (Mecca): Represents Abraham and 
Muhammad. 
○ Theme: These symbols represent one continuous message delivered 
through different messengers. 
● The "Missing" Verse 5: 
○ A printing error was discovered in the draft translation where Verse 5 
was missing in both English and Arabic. 
○ Lesson on Preservation: Dr. Khalifa uses this to teach that the Quran 
is not "ink and paper." He references the mathematical code (the 
number 12,692 on the wall representing the total sum of verse 

numbers). This total is divisible by 19 only if the missing Verse 5 is 
included and the two "false verses" (9:128-129) are excluded. This 
proves the missing verse belongs, even if a printer drops it. 
● "The Best Design" vs. "Lowest of the Low": 
○ Physical Design: Hamid demonstrates the importance of the opposable 
thumb and human balance (walking on one leg at a time). 
○ Spiritual Design: Humans started in a high society (best design) but 
were reverted to the "lowest of the lowly" (this world) due to their 
decision to side with Satan. 
○ Redemption: Humans have the capacity to rise from this low state 
through belief and righteousness. 

2. Botanical & Scientific Discussion 
● Figs and Olives: 
○ Hamid notes that figs can produce two crops a year, whereas olives 
often alternate bearing (heavy crop one year, light the next). 
○ Health Benefits: It is noted that olive oil is unique because it helps 
reduce cholesterol, unlike many other fats. 
● Chemical Isomers (Chirality): 
○ Dr. Sabahi (a chemist) discusses the complexity of plant chemistry. 
○ The "Glove" Analogy: He explains that synthetic chemists struggle to 
replicate plant molecules because of Chirality (handedness). A 
molecule can have a "right-handed" and "left-handed" version (mirror 
images). Plants naturally produce the effective version, while synthetic 
versions often lack potency because they cannot perfectly replicate this 
orientation. 

3. Theological Questions (The "Why Create Us?" Debate) 
● The Question: Robert asks: If God knew the majority of humans would fail 
and go to Hell, why create them at all? 
● The Answer (Second Chance Theory): 
○ Dr. Khalifa explains that humans already existed and committed a 
"crime" (siding with Satan). 
○ This life is a Second Chance. Without this life, humans would have 
gone straight to Hell. 
○ The "Worth It" Logic: It is worth creating the universe to save the 
millions who do succeed. 
● Specific Group Statistics (Somalia): 

○ Dr. Khalifa uses Somalia as an example of God's mercy regarding the 
age of responsibility (40 years old). 
○ He states that while the situation in Somalia is tragic, the majority of 
Somalians dying before the age of 40 are going to Heaven because they 
die before reaching the age of full accountability. 

4. Sura 96:1–19 (The Embryo) 
● The First Revelation: These were the first verses revealed to Muhammad in 
the cave. 
● Translation Debate ("Clot" vs. "Embryo"): 
○ A debate occurs regarding the translation of the word 'Alaq. 
○ Dr. Bucaille's View: Dr. Khalifa mentions meeting Dr. Maurice Bucaille 
(author of The Bible, The Quran, and Science), who was "very angry" 
at translators using the word "Clot" because a clot is dead blood, 
whereas an embryo is living, dividing cells. 
○ Linguistic Meaning: The word literally means something that "hangs" 
or "suspends" (like a leech), which accurately describes the 
implantation of the zygote in the uterus. 
○ Consensus: "Embryo" is the preferred translation over "Clot." 
● The Pen: Verse 4 mentions God teaches by means of the pen. This highlights 
the power of literacy and written records in human advancement and 
religion. 
● Transgression of the Rich: 
○ The Sura warns that humans transgress when they perceive 
themselves as "rich" (independent/self-sufficient). 
○ Dr. Sabahi warns that wealth (financial or otherwise) often leads to ego 
worship. 
● Preventing Prayer: 
○ The Sura condemns those who forbid others from praying. 
○ Dr. Sabahi draws a parallel to pre-revolution Iran, where praying was 
mocked as "uncivilized," versus post-revolution Iran, where it became 
forced/political. 

Administrative & Closing Notes 
● Next Schedule: 
○ Next week: Lory will teach up to Sura 105. 
○ Following week: Ahmad Rayan will finish the Quran (Suras 106-114). 
● Al-Fatihah Recitation: The group recites Al-Fatihah for: 
○ Philip and Evelyn (Evelyn traveling to Oregon). 

○ Ibi Abib (Son of Mahmood and Linda). 
○ Catherine (Birthday tomorrow). 
○ Martha (Birthday in absentia). 
○ Maryam (Offering thanks).

title: Quran Study 3
content:
Quick Notes for Quran Study 3 - Study Information 

● Study Leaders: 
○ Dr. Rashad Khalifa: Leads the first half (Suras 10 and 23) and 
presents the mathematical presentation on the word "God." 
○ Dr. Mahmood Sabahi: Leads the second half (Sura 3). 
● Date of Recording: 01/19/1990 & 01/26/1990 

Quran Verses Discussed 
● Sura 10 (Jonah): Verses 79–92 
● Sura 23 (The Believers): Verses 1–14 
● Sura 3 (The Family of Imran): Verses 110–117 
● Reference Verses: 
○ Sura 72:13 (No fear for believers) 
○ Sura 28:7 (Moses' mother) 
○ Sura 3:81 & 33:7 (The Covenant of the Prophets) 
○ Sura 2:60-61 (Moses and the water/food) 

Detailed Summary of Discussion 
1. Sura 10:79–92 (Jonah) – History & Preservation 
● God's Timing: Dr. Khalifa discusses the parting of the Red Sea. While 
scientists may explain it via geological phenomena, the miracle lies in the 
timing—it happened exactly when Moses needed it. 
● Trust in God: The discussion highlights the immense trust required of Moses' 
mother to throw her baby into the river, knowing God controls all outcomes. 
● Pharaoh's Belief & Death: 
○ The "Too Late" Principle: Pharaoh declared belief in God while 
drowning (10:90), but it was rejected (10:91). Dr. Khalifa explains that 
belief alone is insufficient without the development of the soul (via 
contact prayers, charity, etc.) accumulated over time. 
○ Preservation of the Body: Verse 10:92 states Pharaoh’s body would be 
preserved as a sign for future generations. 
○ Mummies: The group discusses visiting the Cairo Museum. Dr. Khalifa 
notes the irony that the Arabs had no knowledge of mummification 
when the Quran was revealed, yet the Quran accurately predicted the 
body's preservation. 
○ There is a debate on the identity of the Pharaoh; Dr. Khalifa suggests 
it is likely Merneptah, though popularly identified as Ramses II. 

2. Sura 23:1–14 (The Believers) – Traits & Embryology 
● Traits of Success: Successful believers are defined as those who are humble in 
their Contact Prayers (Salat), avoid vain talk, give charity (Zakat), maintain 
chastity, and are trustworthy. 
● Mathematical Structure of Prayer: Dr. Khalifa mentions the number of units 
(Rak'ahs) in daily prayers totals 17 (2+4+4+3+4). He notes that this total (17) 
is part of a mathematical code, and missing a prayer disrupts the pattern 
(e.g., missing Fajr drops the total to 15). 
● Embryology: 
○ Verse 14 describes the development from a drop to a "hanging embryo" 
to a "bite-size fetus" (Mudghah). 
○ Translation Note: Dr. Khalifa prefers "bite-size" or "chewed lump" to 
describe the fetus at this stage, noting it looks like a piece of meat with 
teeth marks. 
○ Memory & Soul: A discussion ensues about why humans don't 
remember their birth. Dr. Khalifa explains that the physical brain has 
limited storage and pushes early memories to the subconscious, but the 
Soul (the "black box") records everything. 

3. The Mathematical Miracle: The Word "God" (Allah) 
Dr. Rashad Khalifa presents a specific set of mathematical discoveries regarding the 
word "God" (Allah) in the Quran to demonstrate its divine authorship and the 
specific rejection of the two "false verses" in Sura 9. 
Key Statistics Presented: 
● Total Count: The word "God" occurs 2,698 times in the Quran (19 x 142). 
● Sum of Verse Numbers: The sum of all verse numbers containing the word 
"God" is 118,123 (19 x 6,127). 
● Multiples of 19: The count of the word "God" in verses that are multiples of 
19 is 133 (19 x 7). 
● Initialed Section: From the first initialed Sura (2) to the last (68), the count of 
the word "God" is 2,641 (19 x 139). 
● Un-initialed Section: The count in the rest of the book is 57 (19 x 3). 
Proof Regarding Sura 9 (127 vs. 129 Verses): 
● Suras ending in digit 9: Taking all Suras where the number of verses ends in 
9 (e.g., Sura 10 has 109, Sura 15 has 99), the total count of the word "God" in 
them is 190 (19 x 10). This only works if Sura 9 is counted as 127 verses. 
● Suras ending in digit 7: Taking all Suras where the number of verses ends in 
7 (e.g., Sura 1 has 7), the total count of the word "God" in them is 209 (19 x 
11). This only works if Sura 9 is counted as 127 verses. 

● Cumulative Count: The count of the word "God" from the beginning of the 
Quran to the end of Sura 9 (verse 127) is 1,273 (19 x 67). 
● Sura 9 Checksum: Sura Number (9) + Number of Verses (127) + Count of 
word "God" in Sura 9 (168) = 304 (19 x 16). 

4. Sura 3:110–117 (The Family of Imran) – Community & Society 
● The Best Community: Dr. Sabahi teaches that the "Best Community" is 
defined by advocating righteousness, forbidding evil, and belief in 
God—regardless of race or nationality. 
● Unity: Emphasizes holding fast to the "rope of God" (3:103) and avoiding 
division. 
● Social Commentary (Switzerland): 
○ Dr. Sabahi references a 60 Minutes documentary about Needle Park in 
Zurich. 
○ He contrasts the external cleanliness and wealth of Switzerland with 
the moral decay of youth addiction and hopelessness. 
○ He notes that wealth without morality leads to spiritual emptiness, 
where the only goal becomes the "next injection." 
● Righteous People of Scripture: Verse 113 acknowledges that not all followers 
of previous scriptures are wicked; some recite God’s revelations at night and 
fall prostrate. 
○ Rashad's Clarification: While these good deeds are rewarded (3:115), 
Dr. Khalifa clarifies that without the specific rites of the Contact 
Prayers (Salat) and Fasting (which many Christians/Jews have lost or 
altered), the soul does not grow sufficiently for the highest ranks. 

Administrative & Personal Notes 
● The "Pill" Mistake: Dr. Khalifa apologizes to Muhtesem for a theological 
slip-up the previous day. He had handed Muhtesem medicine saying, "These 
pills will heal you." He corrects himself to say that only God heals, and the 
pills are merely a mechanism/tool. 
● Cats: The session opens with lighthearted talk about the cats (Behrouz, 
Ismail) and their interactions.

title: Quran Study 4
content:
Quick Notes for Quran Study 4 - Study Information 

● Study Leaders: 
○ Dr. Rashad Khalifa: Leads the commentary on Suras 37 and 10. 
○ Dr. Mahmood Sabahi: Leads the commentary on Sura 3. 
● Date of Recording: 01/21/1990 & 01/22/1990 

Quran Verses Discussed 
● Sura 37 (The Arrangers): Verses 1–69 
● Sura 10 (Jonah): Verses 43–54 
● Sura 3 (The Family of Imran): Verses 118–129 
● Reference Verses: 
○ Sura 90:4 (Humans created for hard work) 
○ Sura 7:172 (The primordial witness of God) 
○ Sura 44 (The Smoke) 

Detailed Summary of Discussion 
1. Sura 37:1–69 (The Arrangers) 
● Entering Hell (Humorous Survey): 
○ Dr. Khalifa and the group jokingly brainstorm "methods" disbelievers 
use to force their way into Hell (insisting on entry despite God's 
mercy). 
○ The List: Storming the gates, tunneling under the fence, pole vaulting, 
doing somersaults (circus style), and being shot out of a human 
cannon. 
○ Theological Point: Disbelievers insist on Hell; God does not want them 
there, but they break through the barriers (like the number 19) to get 
in. 
● "The Blamers" (Az-Zajirat): 
○ A discussion on the translation of verse 37:2. Ismail jokingly told a 
critic it meant "Goats" to silence him. 
○ Actual Meaning: Rashad explains these are angels who blame 
disbelievers ("We served you, yet you disbelieved"). 
● Lord of the Easts (Astronomy): 
○ Debate over the translation of Mashariq (Easts). It is defined as the 
"risings" of heavenly bodies (Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Moon, Sun). 
● Creation & The Shahada: 
○ Wet Mud: Humans were created from "wet mud" (Teen Lazib), 
described as malleable, sticky clay (clay + water). 

○ The Shahada: Dr. Khalifa argues the testimony (Shahada) should only 
be La ilaha illa Allah. He cites Sura 7:172, stating that souls witnessed 
God's Lordship before creation, but never witnessed Muhammad. 
Therefore, witnessing Muhammad is technically a "lie" because the 
soul did not see it. 

2. Sura 10:43–54 (Jonah) – The Asteroid  
● H. Jay Melosh Article: 
○ Dr. Sabahi reads an article from Nature magazine by planetary 
scientist H. Jay Melosh. 
○ The Theory: An asteroid/comet impact hit Earth, vaporizing rock and 
creating a firestorm that broiled the planet (killing dinosaurs). 
○ The Connection: Dr. Khalifa connects this scientific theory to the 
"Smoke" prophesied in Sura 44, saying a similar asteroid impact would 
trigger the end of the world/Hell on Earth. 
● Communities/Congregations: 
○ Verse 47 mentions every "community" (Ummah) has a messenger. The 
group clarifies Ummah refers to a religious congregation (e.g., 
Baptists, Muslims) rather than a neighborhood. 

3. Sura 3:118–129 (The Family of Imran) 
● Hypocrites & Outsiders: 
○ Warning: Believers are told not to befriend outsiders who wish them 
harm (3:118). 
○ Biting Fingers: A sign of the hypocrites' rage is "biting their fingers" 
when they leave the company of believers. This is described as a 
psychological manifestation of deep anguish and hatred. 
● The Battle of Badr (Statistics): 
○ God supported the believers with 3,000 and then 5,000 angels 
(3:124-125). 
○ Dr. Khalifa's Note: He urges the group to check the Encyclopedia 
Britannica regarding the Battle of Badr. He states that historically, the 
disbelievers outnumbered the believers significantly (citing a ratio of 
roughly 10 to 1 in equipment/camels). 
● Strength of Faith: 
○ Dr. Sabahi relates a story about the Black Muslim movement (Nation 
of Islam context) in Brooklyn. He notes that when these individuals 
found faith (even in early stages), they gained immense strength and 

confidence, allowing them to walk fearlessly into dangerous areas 
(drug zones) where others were afraid. 

Administrative & Personal Notes 
● Ramadan & Moon Sighting: 
○ The group criticizes the traditional method of visual moon sighting, 
calling it "dumb" in the age of astronomy. 
○ Rashad notes that the Washington Post publishes exact moon/planet 
rise times, yet religious leaders still confuse the dates every year 
(Pakistan and India often celebrating Eid on different days). 
● Lydia's Exam: Mention is made of Lydia's sister taking her ECFMG (medical) 
exam on Tuesday; the group agrees to read Al-Fatihah for her success.

title: Quran Study 5
content:
Quick Notes for Quran Study 5 - Study Information 

● Study Leaders: 
○ Lisa: Leads the reading and commentary on Suras 56 and 57. 
○ Dr. Rashad Khalifa: Provides extensive commentary, theological 
interpretations, and presents the mathematical miracle data. 
● Date of Recording: 02/17/1989 

Quran Verses Discussed 
● Sura 56 (The Inevitable): Verses 75–96 
● Sura 57 (Iron): Verses 1–5 
● Reference Verses: 
○ Sura 12:24 (Joseph diverted from sin) 
○ Sura 46:15 (Age of 40/Maturity) 
○ Sura 41:44 (Understanding the Quran) 
○ Psalm 8:3-4 (Biblical reference regarding the heavens) 

Detailed Summary of Discussion 
1. Sura 56:75–96 (The Inevitable) – Astronomy & Preservation 
● The Oath of the Stars (56:75-76): 
○ God swears by the "positions of the stars," calling it an awesome oath. 
○ Scientific Context: Lisa and Rashad read scientific data to 
contextualize the "awesomeness" of this oath. 
■ The Milky Way is 100,000 light-years across. 
■ The nearest galaxy is 2 million light-years away. 
■ There are billions of galaxies. 
○ Biblical Reference: Lisa quotes Psalm 8, asking "What is man that You 
should be mindful of him?" given the vastness of the heavens. 
● Preservation & "Touching" the Quran (56:77-80): 
○ "None can touch it": The group discusses the traditional misconception 
that this verse means one must perform ablution (wudu) to physically 
touch the book. 
○ Correct Interpretation: It refers to intellectual access. Only the 
sincere/righteous can understand the deep meanings and the 
mathematical code. The insincere are blocked by God from "touching" 
the truth of it. 
○ Names of the Quran: Rashad notes the Quran is described with God's 
own attributes: Karim (Honorable), Azim (Great), and Majid 
(Glorious). 

● The Mathematical Miracle Presentation: 
○ Dr. Khalifa circulates a document summarizing the Code 19 miracle to 
prove the Quran's preservation. 
○ Simple Facts: 114 Suras (19x6), First Verse is 19 letters. 
○ The "Circle" Discovery: Rashad explains a complex mathematical 
discovery (the "Longest Number"). 
■ It involves writing the verse numbers of a Sura followed by the 
total number of verses in that Sura, for all 114 Suras (e.g., 1, 2, 
3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 7). 
■ This creates a number with 12,696 digits which is a multiple of 
19. 
■ Abdullah’s Addition: Abdullah discovered that inserting the 
Sura Number at the beginning, middle, or end of the sequence 
still results in a number divisible by 19. 
■ Constraint: This calculation only works if Sura 9 is counted as 
127 verses (rejecting the two false verses). 
● The Three Groups & The "First Generation" (56:88-96): 
○ The verses describe the destinies of three groups: Those closest to God 
(High Heaven), Those on the Right (Lower Heaven), and the Rejectors 
(Hell). 
○ The High Heaven (First Generation): Rashad explains that the "First 
Generation" refers to the pioneers who stand with a messenger during 
persecution (e.g., those with Abraham, those with Muhammad in 
Mecca, and the current group with Rashad). Those who "jump on the 
wagon" later when it is easy do not get the same credit. 
○ The Lower Heaven (Age 40): Rashad discusses why some people die 
young (e.g., Martin Luther King Jr., Malcolm X). 
■ Theory: God takes them before they reach the age of 40 (the age 
of full responsibility) to save them. Had they lived longer, they 
might have been "swept by the crowd" into idolatry (e.g., 
worshipping Jesus). By taking them early, God mercies them 
into the Lower Heaven. 

2. Sura 57:1–5 (Iron) – God’s Omnipotence 
● Glorification: Everything in the universe glorifies God physically (atoms, 
cells). Humans are the only creatures who must choose to glorify Him 
mentally. 
● Absolute Control: 
○ God controls life, death, and every atom. 

○ Practical Application: Lisa emphasizes that while we take medicine or 
vitamins, we must realize God is the one controlling the outcome. God 
controls bosses, spouses, and neighbors. 
● Righteousness is a Gift: 
○ Referencing Sura 12:24, Rashad notes that Joseph did not refrain from 
sin solely by his own willpower; God diverted sin from him because he 
was a devoted servant. Similarly, Abraham was granted 
understanding. Righteousness is a gift from God to those who choose 
Him. 
3. Closing Activity 
● Children's Song: The session concludes with a group performance of a 
children's song titled "Remember God." 
○ Lyrics: "When you see a flower, say Ma Sha Allah... To plan something 
tomorrow, say In Sha Allah... Before you start anything, say 
Bismillah... In everything you try to think, say Alhamdulillah."

title: Quran Study 6
content:
Quick Notes for Quran Study 6 - Study Information 

● Study Leader: Donna (Reads the verses). 
● Date of Recording: 03/10/1989 

Quran Verses Discussed 
● Sura 59 (Exodus): Verses 5–24 (The end of the Sura). 
● Reference Verses: 
○ Sura 33 (Battle of the Parties/Confederates) 
○ Sura 6:159 (Sects in Islam) 
○ Sura 3:103 (Holding fast to the rope of God) 
○ Sura 4 (Hypocrites in the lowest pit of Hell) 
○ Sura 12:103 (Most people will not believe) 
○ Sura 2:186 (God is near/Ramadan) 

Detailed Summary of Discussion 
1. Sura 59:5–8 (War, Spoils, and Divine Protection) 
● God’s Control: God controls the actions of disbelievers and sends angels to 
protect believers. 
● The Exodus (Banishment): 
○ Historical context: The tribes of Arabia united to wipe out Islam, 
overwhelming the small minority of believers. 
○ Terror in Hearts: God cast terror into the hearts of the enemies, 
causing them to flee and leave their homes/lands without a fight. 
● The "Invisible Giant": 
○ Dr. Khalifa uses the metaphor of an "Invisible Giant" (angels) standing 
by every believer to protect them. 
○ Scientific Analogy: He compares the invisible angels to the 
Electromagnetic Spectrum. Humans only see a tiny fraction (visible 
light). Just because we cannot see UV rays, X-rays, or Infrared, doesn't 
mean they don't exist. 
● Spoils of War: 
○ Wealth shouldn't be monopolized by the rich; it must be distributed to 
the poor, needy, and relatives. 
○ Sectarian Abuse: Dr. Khalifa notes how the Shia sect abuses the 
"one-fifth" rule (Khums) to give money to turbanned religious leaders, 
and how both Sunnis and Shias abuse the verse "take what the 
messenger gives you" to justify following Hadith instead of the Quran. 

2. Sura 59:9–10 (The Believers & Immigrants) 
● Community Support: The verses praise those who welcome immigrants and 
share their wealth without hesitation. 
● Real-Life Examples in Tucson: 
○ Emily: Dr. Khalifa mentions Emily, who moved to the community with 
nothing. The community anonymously filled a drawer with envelopes 
of money to support her until she found work. 
○ Lori’s Accident: Lori was thrown from a car during an accident but was 
completely unharmed, while her sister (the driver) was hospitalized. 
This is cited as proof of the "Invisible Giant" protecting a believer. 
● Removing Hatred: The prayer in verse 10 asks God to remove hatred. This 
was historically relevant for enemies who had killed each other's families 
before converting to Islam, now living as brothers. 

3. Sura 59:11–17 (Hypocrites & False Promises) 
● Hypocrites vs. Disbelievers: 
○ Definition: A disbeliever admits they don't believe. A hypocrite claims 
to believe but does not. 
○ Ranking: Hypocrites are worse than disbelievers (lowest pit of Hell) 
because they are deceptive and damaging from within. 
○ Behavior: They promise to support disbelievers but flee when trouble 
starts. They fear people more than God. 
● Political Commentary (Iran): 
○ Khomeini: Cited as a prime example of a hypocrite—sincerely believing 
he is right while acting contrary to the Quran. 
○ Drug Executions: A discussion ensues regarding the execution of 400 
people (drug dealers/addicts) in Iran over 4 weeks. Dr. Khalifa 
condemns this killing in the name of Islam. 
○ Social Issues: Mentions of extreme poverty in Iran leading to parents 
selling children, and high addiction rates. 

4. Sura 59:18–20 (The PRA - Post Retirement Account) 
● Self-Examination: Believers must examine what they have prepared for the 
"Coming Day" (Judgment). 
● The "PRA" Concept: 
○ Dr. Khalifa compares life to school/work. Humans work hard for 40 
years to save about $800,000 for retirement. 
○ The Eternal Future: The Hereafter lasts forever (millions of years). 

○ Deposits: Contact Prayers (Salat) and remembering God are "deposits" 
into the PRA (Post Retirement Account). 
○ Interest Rate: God gives a minimum of 7000% interest on these 
deposits. 
○ Warning: One cannot return to Earth to make deposits once the 
account is closed (death). 

5. Sura 59:21–24 (The Mountain & God’s Names) 
● The Quran's Power: If revealed to a mountain, it would crumble out of 
reverence. Humans should strive to have the submission of a mountain. 
● Design Argument: 
○ Dr. Khalifa asks the group to reflect on the design of the human body: 
the articulation of the arm to scratch an ear, the perfect fitting of upper 
and lower teeth, and fingernails. 
○ "One Mouth, Two Ears": A design feature suggesting humans should 
listen twice as much as they speak. 
● Attributes of God: 
○ God is the King, Sacred, Peace, Faithful, Supreme, Almighty. 
○ Everything in the heavens and earth glorifies Him. 
○ Disbelievers Glorify God: Donna notes that even disbelievers glorify 
God by fulfilling His words/prophecies regarding their behavior. 

Administrative & Closing Notes 
● Next Week: Donna's daughter (referred to as "my daughter" by Rashad) will 
teach Suras 60, 61, and 62 because she is on Spring Break. 
● Historical Correction: Farhad asks about a footnote claiming Muhammad 
was unconscious during revelation. Dr. Khalifa corrects this, stating 
Muhammad was conscious and wrote the Quran with his own hand. 
● The "King and the Bird": Dr. Khalifa tells a Middle Eastern folk tale about a 
King trying to find a thief. The King claims the thief has a feather on his 
head, causing the guilty man to touch his head. This analogy explains why 
fabricators created Hadiths defending the "two false verses"—their guilt 
made them expose themselves. 
● Al-Fatihah: The group recites Al-Fatihah for Matt's birthday, wishing him 
happiness and the fulfillment of his wishes. Dr. Khalifa jokes, "You just 
deposited 10 billion dollars in your PRA account."

title: Quran Study 7
content:
Quick Notes for Quran Study 7 - Study Information 

● Study Leaders: 
○ Catherine: Leads the commentary on Sura 62. 
○ Dr. Rashad Khalifa: Provides historical context, commentary on Sura 
63, and general theological answers. 
● Date of Recording: 03/24/1989 

Quran Verses Discussed 
● Sura 62 (Friday): Verses 1–11 
● Sura 63 (The Hypocrites): Verses 1–11 
● Reference Verses: 
○ Sura 9:128-129 (Referenced as the "two false verses" added 19 years 
after the Prophet) 
○ Sura 81:29 (Will of God) 
○ Sura 5:48 (Different rules for different congregations) 
○ Sura 2:62 (Believers of all faiths go to Heaven) 
○ Sura 46:15 (Age of 40) 

Detailed Summary of Discussion 
1. Historical Announcement: The Pure Quran 
● Corruption of the Text: Dr. Khalifa explains that the original Quran written 
by Muhammad was chronological. 19 years after his death, under Uthman, a 
committee standardized the text but added two false verses to Sura 9 to 
"honor the prophet." 
● New Translation: This session marks the last use of the old translation. Next 
week, the group will use the New Translation (Pure Quran), which removes 
these additions. It will be published as a hardcover blue book with gold 
stamping. 

2. Sura 62:1–11 (Friday) – Worship & Community 
● Nature Glorifies God: Everything (rocks, trees) submits to God. Catherine 
notes humans should strive to be as steadfast as rocks. 
● Donkey Metaphor: Verse 5 compares those who carry scripture but don't 
understand it to a "donkey carrying great works of literature." 
● "Chosen People": Verse 6 challenges Jews (or any group) who claim 
exclusivity to God's mercy. If they were truly chosen and righteous, they 
would long for death (to meet God), but they fear it due to their sins. 
● Friday Prayer (Salat Al-Jumu'ah): 

○ Commandment: Believers must drop all business and hasten to the 
mosque when the prayer is announced on Friday (Verse 9). 
○ Women's Attendance: The group refutes traditional Hadith that 
discourage women from attending Jumu'ah. The Quran says "O you 
who believe," which includes men and women. 
○ Importance: It is a weekly commandment to commemorate God as a 
community. Missing it without a valid excuse is disastrous for the soul. 

3. Sura 63:1–11 (The Hypocrites) – Deception 
● The Hypocrite's Definition: Someone who claims to believe but does not truly 
believe in their heart. 
● The Shahada: Verse 1 states that hypocrites say "We bear witness that you 
are the Messenger of God." God calls them liars because although 
Muhammad is the messenger, they are using this statement to deceive. 
● Wooden Logs: Hypocrites are described as "wooden logs" (Verse 
4)—impressive in appearance but spiritually hollow and uncomprehending. 
● Charity & Death: Verse 10 urges believers to give charity before death comes, 
at which point the soul begs for a short delay to be righteous, but God never 
postpones the end (Verse 11). 

4. Theological Discussions 
● Christianity & Judaism: 
○ Dr. Khalifa asserts that Christians and Jews who believe in God alone, 
the Hereafter, and lead a righteous life will go to Heaven (citing 2:62). 
○ Conflict: A debate arises about whether there is conflict between the 
scriptures. Dr. Khalifa insists there is no conflict in the original 
messages (Torah, Psalms, Gospel, Quran) regarding monotheism. 
○ Dominance of Islam: Dr. Khalifa predicts that within 20–50 years, the 
Quran's mathematical miracle will prove its divine authorship to the 
world, making Islam the dominant religion even in America. 
● Hypocrisy vs. Disbelief: Hypocrites are worse than disbelievers (lowest pit of 
Hell) because they are deceptive from within the community. 
● Iran & Khomeini: The group discusses the situation in Iran, labeling 
Khomeini a "hypocrite" for acting against Quranic principles while claiming 
Islam. They discuss the execution of drug addicts and social decay in Iran. 

Administrative & Personal Notes 
● Birthdays & Prayers: 
○ Laila's Birthday: Celebrated (March 19th). 

○ Al-Fatihah Recitations: 
■ For Soad (upcoming test). 
■ For Ahmad Rayan (PhD exam). 
■ For Jahan (to keep him in Tucson longer). 
● Next Week: Jahan will teach the next session.

title: Quran Study 8
content:
Quick Notes for Quran Study 8 - Study Information 

● Study Leaders: 
○  Lori (Reads the verses) 
○ Dr. Rashad Khalifa (Provides extensive commentary, theological 
explanations, and answers questions). 
● Date of Recording: 04/07/1989 
● Special Announcement: Dr. Khalifa announces that next week they will 
use the New Translation (the "Pure Quran" without the two false verses), 
which will be published in hardcover (blue with gold stamp) in the upcoming 
Ramadan. 

Quran Verses Discussed 
● Sura 65 (Divorce): Verses 10–12 
● Sura 66 (Prohibition): Verses 1–12 
● Reference Verses: 
○ Sura 65:8 (Rebelling against God's law) 
○ Sura 10:11 (God guides believers) 
○ Sura 4:132 (Family Prayer) 
○ Sura 3:47 (Mary's chastity) 
○ Sura 20:132 (Exhorting family to pray) 

Detailed Summary of Discussion 
1. Sura 65:10–12 (Divorce) – Evolution & The Seven Earths 
● Reminder: God sends messengers as a reminder to believers to keep them on 
the straight path. 
● Divorce & Provision: 
○ Discussion on providing for a divorced wife, especially if she is 
pregnant or nursing. 
○ Dr. Khalifa clarifies that a nursing mother can refuse to nurse, and the 
father must then hire a wet nurse. If he demands she not remarry 
while pregnant, he must "put his money where his mouth is" and 
support her. 
● Evolution & The Seven Earths (Verse 12): 
○ Scientific Fact: Dr. Khalifa asserts that evolution is a divinely guided 
process, not random. He mentions the complexity of the fly's eye (4,000 
lenses) remaining constant for millions of years, proving species are 
created independently, though micro-evolution occurs (e.g., navel 
oranges). 

○ The Seven Earths: Verse 12 mentions seven earths. Dr. Khalifa 
explains God created six other planets identical to Earth but lifeless. 
On Judgment Day, atheists/evolutionists will see these lifeless planets 
to prove that life did not randomly evolve just because the conditions 
(water, atmosphere) were right. Life exists on Earth only because it is 
Satan's dominion for the test. 

2. Sura 66:1–5 (Prohibition) – Prophet's Fallibility 
● The Prophet's Mistake: 
○ Verse 1 reprimands the Prophet Muhammad for prohibiting something 
lawful to please his wives. 
○ Theological Point: This proves Muhammad was a fallible human being, 
not infallible. God highlights his errors to prevent people from 
worshipping him. 
● Gossip & Secrecy: 
○ The Prophet entrusted a secret to one of his wives, who spread it. God 
informed him of this betrayal. 
○ Lesson: We must not gossip or break trust. You cannot hide anything 
from God. 
● Divorce: God warns the wives that if the Prophet divorces them, God can 
replace them with better wives (submitters, believers). 

3. Sura 66:6–9 (Family & Repentance) 
● Protecting Family from Hell: 
○ Believers must protect themselves and their families from Hellfire. 
○ Parental Duty: Dr. Khalifa emphasizes the duty to ensure children 
pray. He cites Sura 20:132 ("Exhort your family to pray and persist"). 
○ Discussion: Hamid questions how far one should push children. Dr. 
Khalifa insists that if a parent consistently follows God's command 
from the start, the children will naturally follow without resistance. He 
cites his own children (Sam and Beth) as examples. 
○ Beth's Clarification: Beth clarifies that while they prayed out of 
guilt/duty when young, they later chose it for themselves. Dr. Khalifa 
agrees, noting he never punished them, but persisted in reminding 
them. 
● Repentance: Verse 8 calls for "sincere repentance" (Tawbatan Nasuha). It is a 
chance to wipe the slate clean. 
● Striving Against Disbelievers: Verse 9 commands the Prophet to strive 
against disbelievers/hypocrites. Dr. Khalifa notes this is done through truth 

and sometimes harshness (like the Muslim Perspective newsletter) to wake 
them up before it's too late. 

4. Sura 66:10–12 (Intercession Myths) 
● The Myth of Intercession: 
○ Wife of Noah & Lot: Both were married to prophets but disbelieved and 
went to Hell. Their husbands could not save them. 
○ Wife of Pharaoh: Married to the worst tyrant but was a believer and 
went to Heaven. Her husband's evil did not damn her. 
○ Mary: Cited as an example of chastity and obedience. 
○ Conclusion: There is no intercession. Everyone is responsible for their 
own soul. A prophet cannot save his own wife, nor can a tyrant damn 
his believing wife. 

Administrative & Personal Notes 
● Correction: Poopak found a typing error in the draft translation (missing the 
word "God" in Sura 65:8). It will be fixed. 
● Al-Fatihah: The group recites Al-Fatihah for: 
○ Farhad Moini's Birthday (Thursday). 
○ Soad & Ahmad Rayan (Both passed their exams). 
○ Frank (Taking his state exam). 
● Next Week: Gatut will teach Sura 67.

title: Quran Study 9
content:
Quick Notes for Quran Study 9 - Study Information 

● Study Leaders: 
○ Edip Yuksel (Reads and provides commentary) 
○ Dr. Rashad Khalifa (Provides extensive commentary, scientific 
explanations, and answers questions). 
● Date of Recording: 05/12/1989 

Quran Verses Discussed 
● Sura 70 (The Ma'arij/The Ascensions): Verses 1–44 
● Reference Verses: 
○ Sura 26 (Quran in Arabic/foreign tongue) 
○ Sura 95:4 (Human created in best design) 
○ Sura 32:7 (Perfected everything He created) 
○ Sura 21:38 (Human created hasty) 
○ Sura 4:25 (Permission to marry slaves) 
○ Sura 29:45 (Salat protects from sin) 

Detailed Summary of Discussion 
1. Sura 70:1–4 (Time Relativity & Angels) 
● Relativity of Time: 
○ Verse 4 states angels ascend in a day equal to 50,000 years. 
○ Edip explains that time is relative, not absolute. Just as a fly's 
3-month lifespan feels like a lifetime to it (equivalent to 50 human 
years), divine time operates on a different scale. 
○ Speed of Light: Dr. Khalifa and Edip discuss Einstein's relativity. 
Rashad uses an analogy of traveling with a picture at the speed of light 
to explain how time would stand still, or go backward if exceeding light 
speed. 
○ Scientific Fact: Rashad notes that the speed of light is actually "very 
slow" on a cosmic scale (e.g., light takes 100,000 years to cross the 
Milky Way). 

2. Sura 70:5–18 (The Day of Judgment) 
● Horror of the Day: 
○ The sky will be like molten rocks (or lava) and mountains like fluffy 
wool. 

○ Selfishness: Disbelievers are described as so selfish that they would 
offer their own children, spouses, and tribes as ransom to save 
themselves from the fire (Verses 11-14). 
● Hell Calling: Hell is personified; it calls out to those who turned away and 
hoarded wealth (Verse 17). Edip notes that the Quran often personifies 
objects (Earth, Heavens, Records) to show they have a form of consciousness 
or "speech" (signals). 

3. Sura 70:19–35 (Traits of Believers vs. Disbelievers) 
● Human Anxiety: Humans are created "anxious" (Halu'a). When adversity 
touches them, they are despondent; when wealthy, they are stingy. 
● The Exception (The Worshipers): 
○ Only those who observe Contact Prayers (Salat) are free from this 
anxiety. 
○ Traits: They give to the poor (2.5% Zakat), believe in Judgment Day, 
fear God’s requital, keep their chastity, keep their word/trusts, and 
stand firm in testimony. 
● Chastity & Marriage: 
○ Chastity: Dr. Khalifa emphasizes the critical importance of chastity 
(Verse 29). He announces an upcoming appendix on "Chastity and 
Virginity" for children, warning that violating this law destroys future 
happiness and marriage. 
○ Social Commentary: The group discusses the moral decay in society 
(premarital sex, STDs, AIDS) and the responsibility of parents to guide 
their children against these norms. 
○ "Legally Theirs": Verse 30 mentions relations with spouses or what is 
"legally theirs." Rashad explains this covers all legal forms of union, 
including common law marriage or cultural arrangements where a 
couple commits to live together forever, even without a ceremony. 

4. Scientific & Social Discussions 
● Evolution: 
○ Dr. Khalifa asserts that evolution is a divinely guided process, not 
random. He cites the complexity of the fly's eye (4,000 lenses) as proof 
of independent creation of species, though micro-evolution occurs (e.g., 
navel oranges). 
○ Seven Earths: Sura 65:12 mentions seven earths. Rashad explains God 
created six other lifeless planets identical to Earth to prove to atheists 

on Judgment Day that life does not randomly evolve just because 
conditions are right. 
● Marriage Laws: 
○ A discussion arises regarding marriage responsibilities. Rashad 
clarifies that if a man divorces a pregnant woman, he must support 
her. If she refuses to nurse, he must hire a wet nurse. 
○ Arranged Marriage: Rashad notes that arranged marriages or 
inheriting a brother's widow (if consensual) are valid cultural practices 
if they follow Quranic principles of mutual consent. 

Administrative & Personal Notes 
● New Translation Update: Dr. Khalifa mentions a mistake found by Poopak in 
the new translation (Sura 65:8) which will be fixed. 
● Farsi Translation: Good news is announced that a Farsi translation of 
Rashad's work is underway by Behruz. 
● Next Week: Apamea will teach the next 19 Suras (71–89). 
● Al-Fatihah: The group recites Al-Fatihah to close the session, with a 
reminder to ask God for their dearest wishes.

title: Quran Study 10
content:
Quick Notes for Quran Study 10 - Study Information 

● Study Leaders: 
○ Apamea Bashar (Reads the verses) 
○ Dr. Rashad Khalifa (Provides extensive commentary, theological 
explanations, and answers questions). 
● Date of Recording: 05/19/1989 

Quran Verses Discussed 
● Sura 71 (Noah): Verses 1–28 
● Sura 72 (The Jinn): Verses 1–18 
● Reference Verses: 
○ Sura 20:132 (Exhorting family to pray) 
○ Sura 19:16, 41 (Mentioning Mary and Abraham in the book) 
○ Sura 46:10 (Rabbi Judah the Pious) 
○ Sura 50 (Companion/Jinn witness) 

Detailed Summary of Discussion 
1. Sura 71:1–28 (Noah) – Persistence & Human Nature 
● Noah’s Struggle: Noah preached for 950 years, yet his people persistently 
rejected him, putting fingers in their ears and covering themselves. 
● Human Nature: Dr. Khalifa notes that humans haven't changed since Noah's 
time; people still reject the message with the same excuses. 
● Scientific Miracle (Sun vs. Moon): 
○ Verse 16 describes the moon as a "light" (Noor) and the sun as a "lamp" 
(Siraj). 
○ Explanation: A lamp is a source of light, while the moon is a reflector. 
This distinction is scientifically accurate and confirmed by astronauts 
noting the moon's reflective surface. 
● The Flood: Noah asked God not to leave a single disbeliever on earth because 
they would only breed more disbelievers. The flood wiped them out, creating 
the Dead Sea. 

2. Sura 72:1–18 (The Jinn) – Conversion & The Mosque 
● The Jinns: 
○ Verse 1 mentions a group of jinns who listened to the Quran and 
believed. 
○ Dr. Khalifa’s Interpretation: These jinns are the freed companions of 
humans (e.g., Christians who believed in the Trinity) who wandered 

into Masjid Tucson, heard the Quran and the mathematical miracle, 
and converted to Islam (Submission). 
○ Mathematical Proof: The root word Rashada appears 4 times in this 
Sura. The gematrical value of "Rashad Khalifa" (1230) + Sura number 
(72) + Verse count (28) = 1330, a multiple of 19 (19 x 70). 
● Nature of Jinns: 
○ Companions: Every human has a jinn companion (representative of 
Satan) assigned at birth. This companion tries to mislead the human. 
○ Death: When a human dies, both the soul and the jinn companion are 
freed. The jinn stays on earth for a few hundred years before dying. 
○ Witness: The jinn companion serves as the primary witness for or 
against the human on Judgment Day (Sura 50). 
● Spying on Heaven: Verse 8 mentions jinns trying to spy on heaven but being 
chased by projectiles. Dr. Khalifa links this to a period where rockets/shuttles 
(like the Challenger) failed to launch or exploded (74 seconds), suggesting 
celestial interference visible to jinns. 

3. Chastity & Youth (Discussion with Amir) 
● "Keep Your Chastity": 
○ Dr. Khalifa quizzes Amir on the meaning of chastity. 
○ Definition: Keeping oneself pure for one’s future spouse. 
○ Warning to Youth: He warns the youth against the boyfriend/girlfriend 
culture, stating it violates God's law and leads to misery. He promises 
a happy life to those who resist temptation and wait for marriage. 
○ Appendix: He announces he is writing an appendix on "Chastity and 
Virginity" to help parents teach their children. 

4. Parenting & Prayer (Discussion with Hamid) 
● Exhorting Children: 
○ Hamid asks how far parents should go to make children pray. 
○ Quranic Answer: Sura 20:132 says to "exhort your family to observe 
the Salat and persist." 
○ Experience: Dr. Khalifa shares that by consistently reminding his 
children (Sam and Beth) from a young age, they never refused. Beth 
clarifies that while they prayed out of guilt initially, they eventually 
chose it for themselves. The key is persistence without driving them to 
hate religion. 

5. Sanctity of the Mosque (Verse 18) 

● "The Places of Worship Belong to God": 
○ Verse 18 commands not to mention any other name beside God in the 
mosques. 
○ Discussion: A debate arises about mentioning names like "Rashad" or 
"Abraham" during Khutbas or discussions versus during the Contact 
Prayer (Salat). 
○ Conclusion: In the act of worship (Salat), only God's name must be 
mentioned. In discussions/sermons, names can be mentioned for 
historical lessons (as the Quran does). ideally, Dr. Khalifa wishes for a 
mosque with a separate prayer hall where only God's name is ever 
spoken, distinct from the study hall. 

Administrative & Personal Notes 
● Next Week: Apamea will continue teaching from Sura 73 onwards. 
● Prayer for the Youth: Dr. Khalifa emphasizes the importance of guiding the 
youth (Amir, Poopak, etc.) to ensure their future happiness.
